agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration / Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory
vehicle: Delta IV Heavy + Star 48BV third stage
payload: 685 kg (including 11.43-cm carbon-carbon Thermal Protection System sustaining 1,377 °C at perihelion)
credit: © NASA / JHU APL — public domain. Closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown. First mission to enter the Sun's corona (2021-04-28). Final perihelion 22 on 2024-12-24 at 6.1 M km from the Sun's surface (~9.86 R☉).

links.l: Fox et al. (2016) — Parker Solar Probe Mission and Spacecraft (Space Science Reviews)

launch.vehicle_stage: Star 48BV solid third stage (Delta IV Heavy core + 2 strap-ons)
launch.source: NASA Parker Solar Probe Press Kit (2018-08); Fox et al. (2016). Highest C3 ever achieved for a science payload.

cruise.source: JHU/APL Parker Solar Probe Mission Operations Report. Speed at perihelion 22 (2024-12-24): 192 km/s — the fastest human-made object on record (above schema cap; recorded in i18n description). Mid-course corrections collapsed into Venus gravity assist events.

arrival.source: JHU/APL Parker Solar Probe Mission Operations Report; Venus gravity assists shape the orbit, no chemical insertion burn. Perihelion 22 = 6.9 M km from Sun (above schema km cap; recorded in i18n description).

totals.source: NASA Parker Solar Probe Press Kit (2018-08); seven Venus gravity assists deliver the remaining ~4 km/s of effective ∆v needed to walk perihelion in to 9.86 R☉

events.label: Launch — Delta IV Heavy + Star 48BV
events.description: Cape Canaveral SLC-37B, 2018-08-12. Parker Solar Probe required the highest C3 ever achieved for a science mission (154 km²/s²) to break out of Earth's orbital motion enough to fall into a Sun-grazing trajectory. The third-stage Star 48BV solid motor was a custom addition to the Delta IV Heavy stack.

events.label: Trans-solar injection
events.description: Delta IV Heavy + Star 48BV stack delivers Parker onto a Venus-encounter trajectory.

events.label: Venus gravity assist 1
events.description: 2018-10-03. First of seven Venus encounters that progressively lower perihelion. Each VGA bleeds orbital energy; perihelion shrinks ~3 R☉ per encounter.

events.label: First perihelion (P1)
events.description: 2018-11-05. First close approach to the Sun: 0.16 AU (35 R☉). Parker became the closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown, beating Helios 2's 1976 record.

events.label: Venus gravity assist 4
events.description: 2021-02-20. Fourth VGA tightens perihelion further toward the 9.86 R☉ target.

events.label: First corona entry (P8)
events.description: 2021-04-28. Perihelion 8 dipped below the Alfvén critical surface — the formal boundary of the Sun's corona. Parker became the first spacecraft to enter the Sun's atmosphere.

events.label: Venus gravity assist 6
events.description: 2023-08-21. Sixth VGA prepares the final two record-setting perihelia.

events.label: Closest perihelion (P22) — final design milestone
events.description: 2024-12-24. Christmas Eve eve. Parker reached 6.1 M km from the Sun's surface (~9.86 R☉, 0.046 AU) — the closest any spacecraft has ever been to the Sun. Speed at perihelion: 192 km/s, the fastest human-made object ever. The heat shield's solar-facing surface reached ~1,377 °C; the spacecraft bus behind it remained at room temperature. Parker has not yet been commanded back to Earth contact at the time of writing.
